findings.found: the package "imagecache" is named by http://code.example.test/kestrel-labs/imagecache.git: it is a plain http URL, so the code of the package and the answers of the server travel unencrypted and can be changed on the way
findings.fix: name the package by the https URL of its Git repository; for a private package, give the machines that build a credential for https, or set this rule to warning for the SSH URLs your team agreed on

basis.text: a remote package is named by the URL of its Git repository, written with https in the examples, and its version is taken from its tags
basis.source: Adding dependencies to a Swift package (Swift Package Manager documentation)

basis.text: a remote dependency is a Git URL with a requirement: a minimum version up to the next major, an exact version, a half-open or a closed range, a branch or a revision; a local dependency is a path
basis.source: Package.Dependency (Apple Developer Documentation, PackageDescription)

basis.text: a package that needs authentication can be named by an SSH URL, with keys set up on every machine that builds
basis.source: Building Swift packages or apps that use them in continuous integration workflows (Apple Developer Documentation, Xcode)

findings.own: the URL of a remote package in a manifest or an Xcode project whose scheme is not https: http://, git://, ssh://, the form user@host:path that git reads as SSH, file:// and a text with no scheme; http and git:// travel unencrypted, and an SSH URL needs a key on every machine and names the package differently from its https URL; a team whose private packages need SSH can set this rule to warning

findings.found: the package "imagecache" has the requirement from 2.1.0 here and up to next minor from 2.3.0 in examples/messy/CopperleafOrders.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj:71; the two allow different versions
findings.fix: give the package one requirement in every manifest and Xcode project that declares it, or declare it in one place, such as a local package the app depends on

basis.text: a remote dependency is a Git URL with a requirement: a minimum version up to the next major, an exact version, a half-open or a closed range, a branch or a revision; a local dependency is a path
basis.source: Package.Dependency (Apple Developer Documentation, PackageDescription)

basis.text: upToNextMinor stops before the next minor version, and an exact version is not advised because it can cause conflicts in the dependency graph
basis.source: Package (Swift Package Manager, PackageDescription API on swift.org)

basis.text: Package.resolved records the result of dependency resolution, and the versions in it are used for a top-level package; it is ignored when the package is a dependency of another
basis.source: Resolving and updating dependencies (Swift Package Manager documentation)

findings.own: two declarations of one package identity, in the manifests and the Xcode projects of the folder, whose requirements allow different versions; from: "5.0.0", .upToNextMajor(from: "5.0.0"), "5.0.0"..<"6.0.0" and upToNextMajorVersion 5.0.0 count as one requirement; each declaration after the first that differs is reported, with the place of the first; two locations with one identity are named in the message

findings.found: the package "keychain-store" follows the branch develop: what it resolves to changes with every push to that branch, and a package that depends on a branch cannot be used by a package that depends on versions
findings.fix: depend on a released version, such as from: "1.2.0"; if the package publishes no versions, pin a revision for now and ask its owners for a tag

basis.text: a package with a branch-based or commit-based requirement cannot be used by a package that uses a version-based requirement, so such requirements are removed before a version is published
basis.source: Package (Swift Package Manager, PackageDescription API on swift.org)

basis.text: a branch rule is meant for packages developed together whose versions are not published
basis.source: Adding package dependencies to your app (Apple Developer Documentation, Xcode)

basis.text: Xcode advises the version rule, up to the next major or minor version, a range or an exact version, for a package that follows semantic versioning
basis.source: Adding package dependencies to your app (Apple Developer Documentation, Xcode)

findings.own: a .package call with branch: or .branch(...) in a Package.swift, and a package reference of an Xcode project whose requirement kind is branch; what the branch points at changes with every push to it, so two resolutions of the same commit can get different code

findings.found: the package "featureflags" (code.example.test/orbit-ui/featureflags) is declared, but no Package.resolved of the folder pins it, so its version is chosen anew by each resolution
findings.fix: resolve the packages again (swift package resolve, or File > Packages > Resolve Package Versions in Xcode) and commit the Package.resolved it writes

basis.text: Package.resolved records the result of dependency resolution, and the versions in it are used for a top-level package; it is ignored when the package is a dependency of another
basis.source: Resolving and updating dependencies (Swift Package Manager documentation)

basis.text: Xcode writes Package.resolved with the commit each dependency resolves to, and the file is committed so that everyone uses the same versions
basis.source: Adding package dependencies to your app (Apple Developer Documentation, Xcode)

basis.text: Package.resolved is committed so that CI does not build with unexpected versions, and xcodebuild gets -disableAutomaticPackageResolution so that it uses the file as it is
basis.source: Building Swift packages or apps that use them in continuous integration workflows (Apple Developer Documentation, Xcode)

findings.own: a remote dependency of a manifest or an Xcode project whose identity no Package.resolved of the folder pins, when the folder holds at least one Package.resolved; the files are pooled, so a pin in any of them counts
